title: What should load and render be called?
ask: You called PR 3's tree "rendered" and the middle layer. The repo rules ask you before a rename. Which call returns which layer?

options.label: A. load returns the files as written; render builds the rendered tree (recommended)
options.what: load(...) gives the low level; render(graph) gives PR 3's tree, renamed from ILoaded to IRendered
options.cost: Every PR 3 caller changes load(...) to render(await load(...)), and the API doc is rewritten

options.label: B. load keeps the rendered tree; a new open returns the files
options.what: PR 3 callers stay as they are; open(...) is the low level's entry
options.cost: "load" goes on naming the middle layer, the opposite of how the layers stack

title: When a program edits a line that is read in several places, what changes?
ask: sink.conf is included twice, so its max_count line renders both the leds and the porch sink (a snippet body is the same: once per use). Changing that line to stop using $pixels changes both.

options.label: A. The edit lands on the written line; every place that reads it changes (recommended)
options.what: statement.copies() tells the program how many places read the line before it edits
options.cost: A program that meant "only porch" must notice and write that change itself (for example a set line in porch's include block)

options.label: B. The edit fails unless the program names the places it accepts
options.what: Each edit method takes the copies it is allowed to change; a mismatch throws
options.cost: An extra argument on every edit method, in both languages

options.label: C. Villanelle changes only the chosen place
options.what: It writes a set line into that include's block and a $name into the shared line, so only that place changes
options.cost: A refactoring tool, which belongs to the high level; impossible inside a snippet body

title: How does a program write new values?
ask: setValues and replaceWithText take new values. Should they take villanelle text or plain program values?

options.label: A. As villanelle text (recommended)
options.what: setValues("2400"), setValues(quote(host)), setValues("[1, 2] dev"): the same rule handed-in variables already use; the text says whether a value is a word or a string
options.cost: A program calls quote() to write a string

options.label: B. As plain program values
options.cost: A second rule for which kind a plain value becomes (is "sine" a word or a string?), a choice that belongs to the high level
